SK0230 The with expression or object initializer is empty

A pair of initializer braces that sets nothing: new Foo { } is new Foo(), and x with { } copies a record and changes nothing.

CategoryCleanup
Default severitywarning
ScopeSyntax
Needs a compilationno
Runs under --load=looseyes
Cached per fileyes
Fixyes, review it
Language version floor—
Since2.0

Why

Empty braces read as a list somebody is about to fill in and stay in the file for years after nobody is. new Foo { } is two characters of ceremony over new Foo(). x with { } is more than ceremony — with invokes the record's compiler-generated copy constructor, so it allocates a whole instance in order to produce a value equal to the one it was given.

Example

Instead of:

var options = new JsonSerializerOptions { };
var copy = original with { };

Write:

var options = new JsonSerializerOptions();
var copy = original;

The ReSharper mapping

⚠ ReSharper rates RedundantWithExpression a suggestion and RedundantEmptyObjectOrCollectionInitializer a warning; Skala reports one concept at warning and reading resharper_redundant_with_expression_highlighting therefore lowers both. The severity split is the same observation this rule's fixIsSafe: false records: the empty initializer is nothing, and the empty with is an allocation somebody may have meant.

When it does not fire

⚠ The fix is declared unsafe, and the empty `with` is the whole reason. new Foo { } → new Foo() is a pure deletion with no observable effect at all, but x with { } → x is not: the copy constructor produces a distinct instance, so removing it aliases a clone the author may have written in order to mutate it, and it removes the NullReferenceException a null operand would have thrown. Splitting one concept into two safety classes would have been the alternative; the conservative reading of the whole rule is the cheaper mistake. ⚠ Only the two initializer kinds that mean "and then set these members" are matched. An empty array initializer belongs to an ArrayCreationExpression, which this rule never sees — new int[] { } cannot lose its braces and still compile. An anonymous type is a different node again: new { } has no new () to become. ⚠ A creation with no argument list grows one, because new Foo is not an expression; a creation that already has arguments keeps them, and new() target-typed creation is matched through the same path. ⚠ A comment or a preprocessor directive between the braces withdraws the finding: an empty initializer holding a note is a note about why it is empty, and the fix deletes the braces wholesale.
